Title: Microsoft tools to power Manulife's global transformation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Manulife has renewed and expanded its longstanding partnership with Microsoft under a five-year agreement aimed at accelerating its transformation into an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered organisation.
As part of the expanded collaboration, Manulife has adopted Microsoft 365 E7 Frontier Suite capabilities to drive innovation through secure cloud and AI solutions across its global operations.
The insurer will also expand the use of Microsoft 365 Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and deploy Microsoft Agent 365, a next-generation platform designed to govern, monitor and secure AI agents at enterprise scale.
Manulife chief technology and operations officer Shamus Weiland said the partnership is a critical enabler of Manulife's continued evolution into a truly AI-driven organisation.
"Adopting the Microsoft Frontier Suite represents the next phase of that transformation, giving us the trusted foundation to advance AI across our global operations with confidence.
"It also provides the scale, security, stability and intelligence we need to accelerate innovation and embed AI responsibly across the franchise," he said in a statement.
Microsoft also serves as a foundational partner in Manulife's global enterprise AI platform, which is currently in pilot.
The platform will enable the insurer's data scientists and developers to build, deploy and manage AI and agentic solutions at scale while adhering to common standards for quality, security and cost efficiency.
Built on Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry, the platform provides capabilities ranging from citizen development tools to advanced AI model fine-tuning and monitoring, allowing teams to innovate within a governance framework.
Microsoft Agent 365 will also act as a central registry for AI agents across Manulife, providing a single interface to oversee, govern and manage how the agents operate.
The capability is expected to strengthen the company's enterprise-wide AI governance, observability and risk management framework.
Manulife already has AI-powered agent solutions in production, with more under development.
The partnership builds on Manulife's broader AI strategy, with Microsoft technologies already supporting applications across sales, underwriting and customer service.
These include a sales enablement tool that provides personalised adviser insights across multiple markets, the Quick Quote generative AI underwriting tool launched by John Hancock in the US, and generative AI solutions that support more than 110 million customer calls annually across North America while expanding into Asia.
Beyond customer-facing applications, Manulife said AI-powered workflows and agentic solutions are helping employees access information more quickly, support software development and improve IT operations by streamlining workflows and enhancing productivity.
The insurer said developers using GitHub Copilot have increased productivity by about 30 per cent, helping accelerate software design, development and deployment.
It cited the successful rebuilding of its mortgage renewal application within weeks as one example of the technology's impact.
Manulife expects its AI initiatives to generate more than US$1 billion in enterprise value by 2027, having already achieved US$300 million as of the end of 2025 through productivity and efficiency improvements.
Manulife global chief AI officer Jodie Wallis said responsible innovation must be embedded into the way the company operates as AI becomes more deeply integrated across the business.
She said strengthening governance and monitoring capabilities would enable Manulife to deploy AI securely, transparently and in line with its Responsible AI Principles while maintaining the trust of customers, employees and stakeholders.
Meanwhile, Microsoft Canada president Matt Milton said the partnership would help Manulife expand the use of AI responsibly by combining employee productivity tools with enterprise-grade governance and security capabilities.
The expanded collaboration reinforces Manulife's ambition to become an AI-driven organisation.
The insurer was ranked the top life insurance company in North America and Europe for AI maturity in the Evident AI Insurance Index for two consecutive years.

Title: Abundance Treasures launches asset-backed P2P financing platform
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Abundance Treasures Group Sdn Bhd has launched Abundance Dynamic Securities (ADS), a peer-to-peer (P2P) financing platform specialising in asset-backed guaranteed financing.
ADS connects mid-tier companies seeking larger funding with investors through a secure and transparent platform.
Abundance Treasures is registered with the Securities Commission as a recognised market operator for P2P financing.
The company also signed six memorandums of understanding (MoUs) during the soft launch with Koperasi Tenaga Nasional Bhd, Scrut Auto Sdn Bhd, Finzwerk Management, Stocktalk Holding Sdn Bhd, Pam Biz Financial Sdn Bhd and Hakem Arabi & Associates.
The MoUs establish a framework for strategic collaboration to promote P2P financing, broaden market participation and support the growth of Malaysia's alternative financing ecosystem.
Abundance Treasures general manager Dr Lai Heow Gran said mid-tier companies are important contributors to Malaysia's economy, but their financing needs are not always fully met through existing channels.
"ADS provides eligible companies in this segment with an additional regulated financing option that reflects their scale and business needs," he said in a statement.
Eligible companies can access a broader pool of investors through ADS, including institutional, corporate, sophisticated and retail investors across Malaysia.
This enables businesses to diversify their funding sources and reduce reliance on conventional bank financing.
Companies can apply for financing through the ADS platform by submitting details of their funding requirements and supporting documents for assessment.

Title: Panasonic to shut Shah Alam plant by March next year, 400 jobs affected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd will cease operations at its Shah Alam facility by March 2027 as part of a global restructuring aimed at strengthening the competitiveness of its audio-visual consumer business.
In a statement published on its website, the company said television production at the plant will end by September 2026, while production of Blu-ray Disc players will be transferred to China Hualu Panasonic AVC Networks Co Ltd in China.
Production of Technics-branded Hi-Fi audio products will also end at the Shah Alam facility by February 2027 and be transferred to another Panasonic Group company.
The restructuring is expected to affect about 400 employees before the plant ceases operations by the end of March 2027.
Panasonic said it is working with the relevant authorities, government agencies and the Electrical Industry Workers' Union to support affected employees through job placement assistance and career transition programmes.
The move is part of the group's efforts to optimise its global manufacturing footprint and improve product competitiveness.
However, Panasonic said it will continue manufacturing audio products in Malaysia, while sales and after-sales services for its television and audio products will continue as usual.
The Shah Alam facility currently manufactures Panasonic televisions, Blu-ray Disc players and components for Technics-branded audio products.
Panasonic stressed that Malaysia remains a key regional hub for the group, employing about 12,000 people across manufacturing, research and development, and corporate functions.
"Panasonic will continue investing in Malaysia to support its growth strategy within high-value-added supply chains and remain committed to contributing to the country and local communities," it said.

Title: Rice commercial stocks at 1.25 million tonnes as Mardi ramps up crop research
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's overall rice supply remains at a healthy level, with total trading stocks standing at 1.249 million metric tonnes as of July 14, including a 200,000 metric tonne stockpile capable of meeting national demand for 6.2 months.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the government has strengthened its national contingency plans in response to geopolitical risks, extreme climate change and export restrictions by source countries.
He said this includes ensuring that commercial and buffer rice stocks are maintained at optimal levels for immediate use in the event of disruptions to the country's rice supply chain.
Malaysia currently imports rice from key source countries such as Thailand, Vietnam and India.
"To further safeguard supply, the government, through Bernas, has expanded its import network to include other rice-producing countries such as Pakistan, Myanmar and Cambodia.
"To ensure long-term food security, the ministry is also implementing several measures to boost the country's rice self-sufficiency level (SSR)," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
They include the nationwide rollout of the Smart Sawah Berskala Besar (Smart SBB) programme, which adopts centralised farm management and smart agriculture practices to increase yield per hectare.
He said the ministry is also carrying out soil enrichment and rehabilitation programmes to improve soil structure and nutrient content for more sustainable padi production.
"Efforts are underway to enhance irrigation systems in both granary and non-granary areas through the upgrading and maintenance of water infrastructure to support consistent yields.
"In addition, reforms to the padi and rice industry ecosystem are being introduced, including increasing planting frequency through the "5 Seasons in 2 Years" programme in key granary areas such as Mada and Kada," he said.
Research is also being intensified through Mardi to develop new padi varieties that are more resilient to extreme heat, drought and floods, as well as early-maturing strains to shorten harvesting cycles.
Mohamad said these combined efforts are aimed at ensuring the country's rice supply remains secure amid global uncertainties.

Title: Vape excise duty reaches RM354.51mil as govt reviews controls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of RM354.51 million in excise duty has been collected from electronic cigarette or vape products between 2023 and June 11 this year.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said revenue collected from excise duties on vape products was not a justification for allowing the sale of such products.
"For the period during which excise duty was imposed on electronic cigarette or vape products, the recorded tax collections amounted to RM80.32 million in 2023, increasing to RM111.14 million in 2024 and RM118.93 million in 2025.
"From January 1 to June 11, 2026, collections stood at RM44.11 million, bringing the total excise duty collected during the period to RM354.51 million.
"The health and economic costs arising from vape-related illnesses are estimated at approximately RM369 million annually, which is significantly higher than the excise duty collected from vape products," he said in a written Senate reply.
He added that the ministry was examining a proposal to ban bottled electronic cigarette liquids, which carry a higher risk of being modified or mixed with drugs or prohibited substances.
"Any policy proposals, including a broader ban, will continue to be assessed based on scientific evidence, current data and public health interests," he said.
At present, he said, the government was strengthening enforcement of the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024, particularly concerning persons below 18 years old.
He was responding to Senator Robert Lau Hui Yew, who asked whether the government planned to ban the sale and use of vape products, as well as the amount of tax revenue collected from such products.

Title: Alliance Bank expects Malaysia GDP growth near 5pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Alliance Bank Bhd expects Malaysia's economy to grow towards the upper end of the government's four to five per cent forecast this year, backed by strong tourism, sustained foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows and proactive policy measures.
Group chief executive officer Kellee Kam said the country entered the year from a position of strength, with robust domestic demand and continued business activity helping cushion external uncertainties.
"Malaysia is in a fortunate position. We came into this period from a pretty strong position and have taken a lot of proactive measures to support businesses and consumers," he told reporters after the bank's 44th annual general meeting (AGM).
Kam said record tourism activity and strong FDI inflows have supported consumption and investment, while measures introduced by Bank Negara Malaysia and the government have strengthened the economy's resilience.
He said policymakers had acted early to support liquidity through measures such as adjustments to the statutory reserve requirement and financing support schemes.
While geopolitical tensions in the Middle East remain a risk due to their potential impact on oil prices and global supply chains, Kam said current indicators do not point to significant stress in Malaysia's economy.
On the back of the positive economic outlook, Alliance Bank is targeting loan growth of between 7.5 per cent and nine per cent, including unrated bonds, in the financial year ending March 31, 2027 (FY27).
The bank also expects net interest margin of 2.28 to 2.35 per cent and credit costs of 27.5 to 31 basis points, while maintaining a dividend payout ratio of between 40 per cent and 55 per cent, subject to performance.
Kam said loan growth is expected to be broad-based, supported by demand from the electrical and electronics, manufacturing, construction, commercial property and mortgage segments.
Looking ahead, he said Alliance Bank is preparing the next phase of growth beyond its four-year Accelerate strategy, while continuing to invest in digital banking capabilities, including refreshing its Alliance Online app and introducing virtual credit cards and embedded banking solutions.
Shareholders also approved all seven resolutions tabled at the bank's AGM.

Title: No bullying link to student's attempted jump, police confirm
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Police have ruled out bullying as the cause of a Form Two student's attempt to jump from the second floor of a secondary school here yesterday.
Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said preliminary investigations found that the 14-year-old girl had been diagnosed with schizophrenia in May, a condition known to her parents and the school administration.
He said the student was receiving treatment and being closely monitored at Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital here.
"The student last received treatment on July 14 and is scheduled for a follow-up on Sept 15.
"The school had also referred her to a guidance counsellor for 11 sessions and held five consultation sessions with her parents," he told a press conference at the Terengganu police headquarters today.
Also present was Terengganu Education Department Student Development Sector deputy director Mohd Zulkafli Jusoh.
Khairi said the school had taken several measures to ensure the student's safety, including placing her in a ground-floor classroom, having guidance counsellors monitor her daily and asking classmates to accompany her at all times.
He said police school liaison officers would also continue monitoring the case as a preventive measure.
"The public is also advised not to upload or share photos, videos or related content on social media, as this disrespects the victim and her family. Such actions could result in prosecution under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act," he said.
He reiterated that investigations found no evidence linking the incident to bullying and urged the public to refrain from making unfounded allegations.
"All parties are urged to respect the privacy of the student and her family to allow the hospital to continue her treatment while police monitor the case," he said.

Title: Sentence no effect on Shafie as Senallang rep, says speaker
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The five-week jail sentence on former Sabah chief minister Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal does not affect his position as Senallang assemblyman.
Sabah Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Seri Kadzim A. Yahya said the sentence imposed on the Parti Warisan president does not have any effect on his status as an assemblyman for the time being.
"If it is a jail sentence, there is no effect. I don't know whether there was also a fine imposed by the court. If there was a fine, but it is below RM2,000, there would also be no effect.
In Malaysia, an assemblyman can be disqualified from their seat if they are sentenced to more than 12 months in prison, or fined RM2,000 or more, unless they receive a pardon or successfully appeal within the legal timeframe.
"In any case, if the sentence is still being appealed, his position remains status quo and there is no effect for now," he said today.
Earlier, it was reported that Shafie, who is Parti Warisan president, was sentenced to five weeks' jail after he was found guilty of contempt following his remarks on the inquest into the death of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir.

Title: Shafie's remarks 'cannot be shielded under the guise of free speech'
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sessions Court today ruled that Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal's remarks on the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir were not protected by the right to free speech and amounted to serious contempt of court.
Judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan said the court had evaluated the full recording and its context before concluding that Shafie's extrajudicial remarks "cannot be shielded under the guise of free speech".
"Not only has the speech jumped the gun by declaring a verdict of murder before this court has concluded its inquiry, but it has also executed a bullseye shot to the integrity and authority of the administration of justice.
"In short, it is constituted as a serious contempt of court," said the judge in his decision today.
Amir Shah said whether the coroner would be influenced by the respondent's (Shafie's) statement was "immaterial and irrelevant", as the issue should not be on the coroner, but on the respondent who made it in public while the inquest was ongoing.
He said the respondent knew, or ought to have known, that the purpose of the inquest was to determine, among other things, the manner in which the deceased came to her death.
The court was satisfied that the attorney-general (the applicant) had established beyond reasonable doubt that the respondent uttered the impugned words on Sept 20, 2025.
Amir Shah said Shafie's words had directly prejudged the central issue of the inquest by stating "This child was murdered" and scandalised the judicial process ("supposedly for the court to investigate... Where is the justice?")
"The statements created a real and substantial risk of interfering with the administration of justice and eroding public confidence, especially in the judiciary.
"The respondent has completely failed to purge the contempt, allowing the offending publication, as far as the court is concerned, to remain publicly accessible," he said.
Earlier,
Shafie was found guilty
of contempt of court. However, the court allowed the sentence to be stayed pending appeal.
The A-G filed an application for leave on Oct 19, 2025, to initiate contempt
proceedings against Shafie,
which was allowed by the court on Oct 23, 2025.
Mohamad Mustaffa  P. Kunyalam and Nadia Mohd Izhar appeared for the A-G, while Jakariya A.B. Jalil and Chen Ket Chuin represented Shafie.

Title: Malaysia told to reinvent Islamic finance to stay ahead
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's next challenge in Islamic finance is no longer building scale, but strengthening innovation as the industry seeks to expand beyond traditional banking and capital market offerings, the central bank said.
Deputy governor Adnan Zaylani Mohamed Zahid said the country's comprehensive Islamic finance ecosystem has made it a global leader, but sustaining that position will require continued innovation and collaboration.
"Our domestic strength is very strong and it will only grow because we expect our financial sector to continue to grow," he said during a panel session at Bank Negara Malaysia's Sasana Symposium 2026.
Adnan said Islamic banking assets account for close to half of Malaysia's banking sector, while the Islamic capital market represents more than 60 per cent of the overall capital market.
He said the country's success was driven not only by its scale, but also by its ability to develop innovative solutions, including social finance initiatives that combine financial services with broader socioeconomic outcomes.
One example is iTekad, a programme that combines social funds, particularly zakat and donations, with financing, training and business support to help microentrepreneurs build sustainable businesses.
"iTekad has garnered international attention for the way we combine social funds, particularly zakat and donations, with financial sector offerings," he said.
He said the programme demonstrates how Islamic finance can address community needs while creating pathways for businesses to grow.
Adnan also highlighted the government's recent US$1.5 billion sovereign sukuk issuance based on sukuk manfa'ah as another example of innovation to broaden Islamic capital market offerings and attract international investors.
The issuance attracted demand of about 4.7 times the amount offered and achieved the government's tightest-ever spread, reflecting strong investor confidence, he said.
He added that the sovereign sukuk would provide a benchmark for Malaysian companies seeking to raise foreign currency funding through sukuk and other financing instruments.
"It helps sukuk issuers and other corporate issuers in Malaysia benchmark their foreign currency fundraising against the sovereign issuance," he said.
Adnan said maintaining Malaysia's leadership in Islamic finance would require regulators, financial institutions and industry players to continue developing new products and solutions.
He added that social finance, talent development and international collaboration would remain key priorities as global competition intensifies.

Title: Many young Malaysians can't tell zakat from charity, says Yayasan Hasanah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Growing gaps in Islamic financial literacy among younger Malaysians have raised concerns, with many unable to distinguish zakat from other forms of charitable giving, Yayasan Hasanah said.
Managing director and trustee Siti Kamariah Ahmad Subki said strengthening basic religious and financial knowledge is essential to help younger generations better understand Islamic finance and make informed financial decisions.
"There are young people who don't understand what zakat is or what it really means. They don't know the difference between zakat and other donations, such as those made to the World Wide Fund," she said during a panel session at Bank Negara Malaysia's Sasana Symposium 2026.
Siti Kamariah said the gap stemmed from a gradual erosion of foundational religious knowledge that underpins Islamic finance.
"The fundamental difference lies in having that basic knowledge, which needs to be reinforced constantly so that people of all generations understand why it matters for their iman and ibadah," she said.
She said improving financial literacy alone would not be enough unless Islamic financial institutions also simplified their products, policies and communication.
"We do have a problem of over-governance in some areas. That's why you need to put people at the centre and understand the problems on the ground, rather than over-engineering solutions," she said.
Siti Kamariah said excessive documentation often creates unnecessary barriers, particularly for small business owners who need practical guidance rather than lengthy explanations.
She also urged businesses to rethink conventional measures of success, saying long-term sustainability should not be sacrificed in pursuit of rapid expansion.
"In business, we often talk about profit maximisation and getting bigger. But we should also recognise the power of staying small, serving local markets well and building businesses that last for generations.
"It requires a mindset shift to value development and growth beyond the traditional focus on profit maximisation," she said.
Siti Kamariah said convenience has also become a key factor shaping consumer behaviour, making digital accessibility essential to encouraging wider adoption of Islamic financial services.
"We have to make it easy for people to take action. I've been paying zakat more regularly simply because it's easy to do through mobile apps.
"I use certain platforms not because I'm disloyal to another bank, but because they're more convenient. People are loyal to what is convenient," she said.
She added that financial literacy initiatives should be communicated in simple, relatable language that ordinary people can easily understand.
"The rule of good communication is that your grandmother should be able to understand what you're saying. We shouldn't over-engineer our messages. We need to make them simple, relatable and engaging," she said.

Title: Penang awaits Kedah's lease claim filing, says Chow
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang is waiting for Kedah to formally file its claim over the state's lease payments before responding, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said.
Chow said the state government has maintained the same position despite Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's latest remarks that all legal and historical documents for the claim are ready.
"I think this is not the first time we have had to answer this. Our answer is the same - we are waiting. That's all," he told newsmen at his office in Komtar here today.
Asked whether pursuing the claim could affect relations between the two states, Chow said it was premature to comment as Penang has yet to receive any formal demand.
"Our view has always been that, in the first place, we do not know what the claim is. For me, it is premature to comment.
"So, we will wait and see what they intend to claim, and we will respond after it is filed in court or submitted to the Penang government," he said.
He was reported as saying that the Kedah government had completed all historical documents, research and legal groundwork related to its proposed review of the lease payment for Penang.
He said the findings had been presented to the state executive council and received its approval to form the basis of the claim, with the state now waiting for the appropriate time to proceed to the next phase.
Earlier this month, Chow said Penang was never consulted on the Sultan of Kedah's call for the federal government to review the state's lease payment.
He said the matter falls under federal jurisdiction as the payment is made by Putrajaya and does not involve the state government.
On July 5, the Sultan of Kedah, Al Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah, called on the federal government to review the lease payment based on current rates, saying the existing payment no longer reflected the spirit and original intent of the agreement.
The Sultan also reminded all parties to respect
Kedah
's rights and sovereignty as enshrined in the Federal Constitution.

Title: Dr Mahathir's RM150mil defamation suit awaits medical update
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The High Court will be updated on Friday on Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad's condition and fitness to resume his RM150 million defamation suit against Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Dr Mahathir's lawyer, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, said a case management would be held online before judicial commissioner Datuk Donald Joseph Franklin.
"Currently, Dr Mahathir is still under the care of the National Heart Institute and it is the experts' opinion that on Friday, they will be able to provide an update on his readiness and fitness to resume the trial.
"It will not be easy due to Dr Mahathir's age and medical parameters," he said.
The two-time former prime minister turned 101 on July 10.
The trial was temporarily halted earlier this year to allow Dr Mahathir time to recover after he suffered a fall while exercising at home.
He was admitted to the National Heart Institute on Jan 6 for observation and treatment.
Rafique had said the incident occurred as Dr Mahathir was stepping off a treadmill after his routine brisk walk before heading to the office.
In his suit, Dr Mahathir alleged that Anwar had tarnished his reputation by accusing him of being racist and enriching himself and his family members during his 22-year tenure as prime minister.
He claimed that Anwar made the statements during a speech at PKR's special national congress at Melawati Stadium in Shah Alam on March 18, 2023.
Anwar had allegedly referred to someone "who in the past had been in power for 22 years and an additional 22 months" as taking advantage of his position to enrich himself and his family.
Dr Mahathir is seeking RM100 million in exemplary damages and RM50 million in general damages, in addition to a written apology and a special press conference for Anwar to apologise for making the statements.

Title: Top 10pct of formal workers earn at least RM11,500 a month
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's top 10 per cent of formal sector employees earned at least RM11,500 a month in March 2026, more than six times the wages of the country's lowest-paid workers.
According to the Statistics Department, employees in the bottom 10 per cent received a monthly wage of RM1,700 or less, while those in the 90th percentile earned at least RM11,500 per month.
The department also reported that 7.9 per cent of Malaysian formal employees earned below RM1,700 a month in March 2026, a decrease of two percentage points from the corresponding month last year.
"This disparity illustrates that employees in the 90th percentile earned more than six times as much as those in the lowest wage group, underscoring the prevailing wage gap between the highest and lowest earners," it said in a statement.
Despite the gap, the department said Malaysia's labour market remained resilient and stable, supported by continued employment growth.
In line with the development, it said the number of Malaysian formal employees increased 3.8 per cent year-on-year to 7.05 million persons in March 2026 compared with the same month of previous year.
Male formal employees, who accounted for 55.0 per cent or 3.88 million of the total workforce, received a median monthly wage of RM3,064, compared with RM3,000 for female formal employees, who represented 45.0 per cent or 3.17 million workers.
By age group, the department said formal employees aged between 45 and 49 continued to record the highest median monthly wage throughout the first quarter of 2026, at RM4,100 in March, RM4,145 in February and RM4,156 in January.
It noted that all age groups recorded positive year-on-year growth in median monthly wages except employees aged below 20 years.
"The highest annual increase was recorded among workers aged 55 to 59, while the median monthly wage for employees below 20 remained unchanged at RM1,700 since February 2025," it said.
By economic activity, the mining and quarrying sector, which accounted for just 0.5 per cent of all Malaysian formal employees, recorded the highest median monthly wage at RM9,678 in March 2026.
In contrast, the agriculture sector, representing 1.8 per cent of formal employees, recorded the lowest median monthly wage at RM2,327, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 5.8 per cent.
Among states, Kuala Lumpur registered the highest median monthly wage at RM4,527, followed by Selangor at RM3,445 and Penang at RM3,064.
Kelantan, Perlis and Sabah recorded the lowest median monthly wages at RM1,827, RM1,855 and RM2,082, respectively.

Title: N9 polls: Kuala Pilah's heritage shophouses await revival
Article:
KUALA PILAH: As polling day draws near, towns and villages across Negri Sembilan are filled with political flags, grand speeches and campaign machinery.
Yet in Kuala Pilah, the pace is noticeably slower.
Away from the election frenzy, rows of ageing shophouses line the town's main street, their weathered facades standing as quiet reminders of a bygone era.
Some are more than a century old, but to longtime residents, they are also among the town's most overlooked treasures.
With proper conservation and restoration, locals believe the royal town could one day rival the heritage streetscapes of George Town and Melaka.
Many of the buildings still bear plaques indicating the year they were built, offering a glimpse into Kuala Pilah's rich architectural history.
The town is also home to a cast-iron post box believed to have been installed before Merdeka, which residents say remains in use to this day.
For 72-year-old trader Lo Chee Yong, the century-old shophouse where he has spent the past 50 years running his business has been in his family for more than 100 years.
"My grandfather bought this place before I was born. It was passed down to my father and now to me. I'm the third generation," he said.
Lo remembers when Kuala Pilah's streets bustled with family-run businesses, but today many young people have left for bigger towns and cities.
"Most of the young people have moved away. The people left here are mostly the elderly.
"If the old buildings are beautified, people will come to see them, just like they do in Penang and Melaka."
Lo highlighted the annual celebration at the century-old Si Thian Kong Temple as proof that Kuala Pilah can attract visitors.
"During the festival, people come from other states and even overseas.
"Hotels are full and some visitors have to stay in Bahau. But it only lasts about 10 days."
Despite keeping the family business alive for decades, none of his four children intends to take over, leaving the future of both the shop and its heritage uncertain.
Just a few doors away, Goh Kok Koon, 66, has a similar story.
His family's business dates back to 1934, spanning more than 90 years across three generations.
"When I was a child, this building was already here. Back then everything was made of wood," he said.
Fearing the ageing structure would deteriorate, Goh renovated the premises about a decade ago, replacing much of the timber with concrete while retaining parts of its original character.
"It wasn't to make it look nicer. We were worried the wood would be damaged."
Goh also believes local authorities should do more to preserve Kuala Pilah's heritage before it disappears.
He lamented that many historic features, including the old post office, railway remnants and a fountain that once stood at the town's roundabout, were either altered or demolished over the years.
"If these places were preserved and their history explained, tourists would come to learn about them and take photographs," he said.
He also believes practical improvements are just as important.
"Business here has dropped because there's not enough parking. If people can't stop their cars, they won't come."
Goh said preserving Kuala Pilah's old streets would not only safeguard its history but also complement attractions such as the more than century-old Si Thian Kong Temple and Sri Menanti, giving visitors more reasons to stay longer in the royal town.
A total of 103 candidates are contesting the 36 state seats, with polling for 867,151 ordinary voters set for this Saturday.

Title: Eppendorf inks lease for first Southeast Asia plant in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: German life science company Eppendorf SE today signed a lease agreement to establish its first Southeast Asia manufacturing facility at Bandar Cassia Technology Park.
This marks the formal commencement of Eppendorf's planned RM180 million (€40 million) greenfield production facility, which is expected to begin operations in 2028 and manufacture selected products from its centrifuges and Instruments portfolio.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the investment reflected the confidence global industry leaders continued to place in Penang's industrial ecosystem while strengthening the state's capabilities in the scientific and measuring equipment sector.
He said the investment would reinforce Penang's position in advanced manufacturing, healthcare and life sciences, while supporting the state's long-term ambition to build a competitive healthcare ecosystem.
"Eppendorf's investment is significant not only for its value, but for what it represents,"
he said at the signing ceremony at Komtar today.
"It reflects the confidence that global industry leaders continue to place in our industrial ecosystem while strengthening Penang's capabilities in Scientific and Measuring Equipment," he added.
Headquartered in Hamburg, Germany, Eppendorf is a global life science company with more than 80 years of history.
Its laboratory products, systems and services support research, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology and diagnostics worldwide.
Chow said Penang had secured RM2.3 billion in approved manufacturing investments in the scientific and measuring equipment sector between 2021 and the first quarter of 2026, representing nearly 20 per cent of Malaysia's total.
The 40 approved projects are expected to create close to 4,500 jobs.
Chow said Penang also remained Malaysia's leading exporting state in 2025, contributing RM611 billion or 38 per cent of the nation's total trade.
Between 2021 and 2025, the state exported RM187 billion worth of professional, scientific and controlling instruments and apparatus, accounting for an average of 72 per cent of Malaysia's exports in the category.
Chow said investments such as Eppendorf's would deepen Penang's industrial capabilities, create opportunities for local companies to move up the value chain and strengthen collaboration between industry, universities and research institutions.
He also encouraged the company to work with local firms through the Penang ATE Campus in technology development, localisation, supplier development and supply chain strengthening.
"The aim is clear: to turn strategic investments into stronger local capabilities and long-term industrial competitiveness," he added.
Eppendorf Group chief executive officer Dr Christine Munz said the Penang project marked another milestone in the company's international expansion strategy and strengthened its long-standing presence in Malaysia, where it established its regional hub in Kuala Lumpur in 1995.
She said the new facility would strengthen Eppendorf's global manufacturing network by creating a production base in Southeast Asia for selected laboratory instruments, including centrifuges, mixers and cyclers.
The company expects the facility to employ about 130 people by the end of 2029, with further expansion planned as production ramps up.
The lease agreement was signed between Eppendorf and the Penang Development Corporation in the presence of representatives from InvestPenang, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority and other government agencies.

Title: Younger customers don't care about Syariah contracts, says Bank Islam CEO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Islamic banks risk losing relevance among younger customers if they fail to deliver seamless digital banking experiences, as consumers increasingly prioritise convenience over the technicalities of Syariah contracts.
Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd group chief executive officer Raja Teh Maimunah Raja Abdul Aziz said banks should focus on delivering customer-centric digital services rather than emphasising the complexity of products behind the scenes.
"I have to caution everybody when it comes to serving the younger generation going forward. I can tell you today, nobody cares about what contract you use. Customer centricity is everything," she said.
Teh Maimunah was speaking at a panel session titled "From Policy to People: Strengthening the Impact of Islamic Finance" at Bank Negara Malaysia's Sasana Symposium 2026 today.
The session was moderated by the central bank's Islamic finance department director Nurul Izza Idris and featured deputy governor Adnan Zaylani Mohamed Zahid and Yayasan Hasanah managing director and trustee Siti Kamariah Ahmad Subki.
Teh Maimunah cautioned that Islamic banks could lose customers seeking Syariah-compliant financial services if their digital offerings become cumbersome or fail to meet rising expectations.
"My fear is that if you get caught up with whatever's in the back end and our delivery becomes frictional, then you will lose people who believe in it," she said.
She said customer experience had become the defining factor for younger consumers, who expect fast, seamless and intuitive digital services.
"If we don't focus on customer delivery, we will lose relevance. Today, it's all about instant gratification. Digitisation is not something you should still be fearful of or not understand, especially when it comes to artificial intelligence," she said.
Teh Maimunah added that many senior decision-makers may not fully understand the expectations of younger customers, whose banking preferences are driven by speed and ease of use.
"Your customers are much younger than you. You may not understand what they're looking for," she said.
She cited the widespread adoption of Touch 'n Go eWallet as evidence that consumers choose financial services based on convenience rather than the technology or contractual structures behind them.
"Why has Touch 'n Go grown by leaps and bounds? Because it's easy to use. They don't ask you how your back-end engineering works. They don't ask what kind of contracts you use.
"As Islamic finance practitioners, we have to make sure everything is Syariah compliant. That is our job. Don't burden customers with questions about whether one contract is better than another. If it's halal, go for it. Just make sure it's frictionless.
"If you fall behind, younger users will simply choose something else, and it may not be Syariah compliant because all they want today is instant delivery," she said.
Teh Maimunah also called on Islamic financial institutions to strengthen their digital capabilities by recruiting talent from outside the Islamic finance ecosystem where necessary.
She acknowledged that younger, digitally savvy customers are increasingly questioning the value proposition of Islamic finance when pricing and customer experience appear similar to those of conventional banks.
"If you don't have the talent within the Islamic finance ecosystem itself, you have to employ people from outside your ecosystem," she said.
"For as long as Islamic financial institutions operate within a fractional banking system, we still have liquidity ratios and capital ratios governed by Basel standards.
"Because we're still bound by the conventional framework, it has a significant impact on how we price our products. We still talk about the same base lending rate or base financing rate. We're still subject to the Overnight Policy Rate. So you have to understand that we cannot be so different," she said.
However, Teh Maimunah stressed that Islamic finance remains fundamentally different through its contractual structures, which are designed to finance real economic activities in accordance with Syariah principles rather than simply lending money.

Title: Senate confirms Jay Clayton as Trump intelligence chief
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Senate confirmed Jay Clayton as Donald Trump's top intelligence official Tuesday, putting a permanent chief in charge of the country's spy agencies as the president revives unsupported election fraud claims ahead of the midterms.
Senators voted 51-47 to confirm Clayton's appointment, with all Democrats in the upper chamber voting against it.
"Jay is outstanding in every way, and will do a spectacular job as Director!" Trump said in a post on Truth Social shortly after the vote.
The former securities regulator and federal prosecutor succeeds Tulsi Gabbard, who resigned last month, and inherits an 18-agency intelligence community shaken by leadership turnover and staff cuts.
His appointment comes as concern mounts that Trump is drawing national security agencies into his effort to relitigate the 2020 election and cast doubt on the integrity of the coming vote.
Earlier this month, Trump used a televised White House address to release declassified intelligence he claimed showed Chinese interference while again falsely asserting that the 2020 election was stolen.
Clayton takes over from acting director of national intelligence Bill Pulte, a Trump loyalist with no relevant experience whose brief tenure alarmed lawmakers in both parties.
Pulte has used his other role as federal housing regulator to refer several of Trump's political opponents for possible prosecution and oversaw sweeping cuts at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.
Hours before Clayton's confirmation vote, Pulte boasted that a fifth round of dismissals would bring staffing reductions at the intelligence coordinating body to about 30 per cent within weeks.
Democrats had initially welcomed Clayton as a more conventional alternative to Pulte, but turned sharply against him during his confirmation hearing.
Repeatedly asked whether Democrat Joe Biden won the 2020 presidential election, Clayton would only say that Biden had been "certified" as the winner.
"I'm not an election denier," Clayton told senators, without directly answering the question.
Senate Intelligence Committee vice chair Mark Warner said he "came away from his confirmation hearing with serious reservations about whether he would be willing to stand up to political pressure."
"I sincerely hope he proves those concerns unfounded, because the Intelligence Community deserves steadier leadership than it has received in recent months," Warner said in a statement after the vote.
Chuck Schumer, the party's leader in the upper chamber of Congress, previously called Clayton's hearing performance "abysmal."
Republicans defended Clayton's record as chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission during Trump's first term and, more recently, as US attorney for the Southern District of New York.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a Republican, said Clayton's experience fighting financial crime and handling national security cases made him a proven leader at a time of heightened threats.
His confirmation could also help revive negotiations over Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which allows the US government to collect communications involving foreigners abroad without an individual warrant.
Democrats had resisted renewing the authority while Pulte remained acting intelligence chief, citing fears of administration overreach.
But any extension is unlikely before September because the House of Representatives has already left Washington for its summer recess.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bridge funding gap for social finance graduates: Bank Negara deputy governor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Entrepreneurs emerging from social finance programmes often face a funding gap as they transition from community-based support to sustainable commercial ventures.
This highlights the need for new risk-sharing models in the country's Islamic finance ecosystem, said Bank Negara Malaysia deputy governor Adnan Zaylani Mohamed Zahid.
Hence, Bank Negara is open to exploring ways to expand the use of risk-sharing instruments to help businesses transition from community-based support programmes into sustainable commercial ventures.
Islamic finance should go beyond providing financial services by creating wider socioeconomic impact, Adnan said.
This includes supporting vulnerable communities, strengthening financial resilience and helping businesses adopt sustainable practices.
He said the central bank's value-based intermediation initiative was introduced to encourage Islamic financial institutions and takaful operators to focus on outcomes aligned with the objectives of Syariah, or Maqasid Syariah.
"Islamic finance wants to do more, and we want it to do more," he said during a panel session on "From Policy to People: Strengthening the Impact of Islamic Finance" at the Sasana Symposium 2026.
Adnan said Bank Negara was willing to consider proposals from industry players on how Islamic financing contracts and instruments could be further developed to better serve businesses and communities.
This includes exploring how regulation could facilitate greater adoption of alternative Islamic financing structures, including risk-sharing contracts.
"We are open to proposals, to ideas on how we can further enhance the delivery of Islamic finance and finance in general," he said.
He added that greater collaboration between regulators, financial institutions and industry players would be needed to develop solutions that address financing needs not fully met by traditional models.
"We are looking at co-creation. It involves collaboration between the central bank and industry, practitioners as a whole, to create products that really meet these various needs," he said.
Adnan said iTekad had expanded significantly since its introduction, growing from an initial 40 beneficiaries in 2020 to more than 14,000 recipients currently.
The programme has also expanded beyond entrepreneurship to include protection and employment initiatives, he said.
Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd group chief executive officer Raja Teh Maimunah Raja Abdul Aziz said entrepreneurs graduating from social financing programmes often faced challenges when moving into commercial financing.
She said programmes such as iTekad had helped beneficiaries grow their businesses, but many continued to be classified as high-risk micro small and medium enterprises when seeking bank financing.
"As they go out to the market, they are still subject to the kind of credit that we look at everybody else. They are deemed to be high risk, rates are expensive," she said.
She said some entrepreneurs ended up paying financing rates of between 12 per cent and 14 per cent, which could slow their progress after receiving initial support.
"Some of them tell us, okay, we got money from you, now we borrow money either from your bank or bank ABCD, and they're charging us 12 per cent, 14 per cent.
"And that unfortunately takes them one to two steps back from where they were," she said.
Teh Maimunah said Islamic financial institutions should consider creating an intermediate financing stage between grants and full commercial financing through structures such as Musharakah and Mudarabah.
Under such models, financiers and entrepreneurs share risks and returns, rather than relying solely on fixed repayment structures.
She suggested developing smaller-scale seed funding based on partnership financing, allowing entrepreneurs to repay gradually while enabling funds to be recycled to support other businesses.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian workers' pay hits record RM686.9bil in 2025
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian workers received a record RM686.9 billion in wages and other employment compensation in 2025, or about one-third of the country's gross domestic product (GDP), the Statistics Department said.
The department said compensation of employees (CE), which measures wages and other employment-related compensation, rose 5.8 per cent from RM649.3 billion in 2024 as the economy continued to expand.
As a result, labour's share of GDP increased to 33.9 per cent from 33.6 per cent a year earlier.
Malaysia's nominal GDP grew 4.8 per cent to RM2.03 trillion in 2025, supported by growth across all economic sectors. The services and manufacturing sectors remained the main contributors, while the mining and quarrying sector continued to contract.
Meanwhile, gross operating surplus, which broadly reflects the income retained by businesses after paying employees, remained the largest component of GDP income at RM1.26 trillion.
However, its share of GDP slipped to 62 per cent from 63.6 per cent in 2024, while growth slowed to 2.1 per cent from 4.9 per cent due to weaker performance in the services, agriculture and construction sectors.
Net taxes accounted for 4.1 per cent of GDP in 2025, up from 2.8 per cent a year earlier, as their value rose to RM83.5 billion from RM54.3 billion.
The department said net taxes grew 53.7 per cent, driven by a 12.9 per cent increase in taxes on production and imports. However, subsidies continued to decline, falling 36.5 per cent following lower petroleum and diesel subsidies.

Title: MACC to stay professional despite negative perceptions, says Abd Halim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will continue to uphold professionalism, transparency and integrity despite negative perceptions surrounding its investigations, Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said.
Such perceptions should not intimidate the agency as long as every investigation was conducted in accordance with the law, procedures and due process, he said.
"We need to prove it through our actions and results. We cannot satisfy everyone.
"In an investigation, those involved may not be satisfied and may form negative perceptions.
"That is their right, but if we carry out our duties according to the law, procedures and the correct principles, we do not need to fear or be intimidated.
"We must carry out our responsibilities with sincerity, honesty and full commitment. Perceptions will always exist, but confidence in the integrity of the process and the professionalism of our officers must be upheld," he said during the MACC podcast Kolar Hitam: Bukan Sekadar Operasi today.
The podcast was hosted by MACC Strategic Communications Division director Hisyam Mohd Yusoff.
Asked about parties questioning MACC investigations before the process was completed, Halim reminded the public to be cautious so that their comments would not be seen as interfering with, influencing or prejudicing investigations.
"The right to express opinions is the right of every individual, but every right has its limits. Section 48 of the MACC Act provides for offences relating to acts that obstruct or interfere with investigations. Therefore, trust the enforcement agencies to carry out their duties.
"It does not mean every complaint lodged with the MACC must be proven true. The MACC's role is to investigate, examine the evidence, consider all angles and make recommendations based on its findings.
"After that, the investigation papers will be referred to the Attorney-General for further consideration and a decision," he said according to Berita Harian.
Halim said that, as chief commissioner, he placed his trust in MACC officers to carry out their duties professionally and impartially, adding that the agency's investigators were competent, certified and gazetted officers.
"After the investigation is completed and reviewed by senior officers, the matter will be referred to the Attorney-General. The MACC recommends the outcome of investigations, but the decision on whether to prosecute rests with the Attorney-General.
"The public must understand this process and should not expect every complaint to result in an outcome that meets the complainant's expectations. The MACC is an independent agency that does not side with any party," he said.
Having led the MACC for three months, Halim said the agency must keep pace with global developments and equip its officers with modern technology, including artificial intelligence, while providing relevant training locally and internationally to enhance their knowledge and skills.
"However, our goal is zero corruption, and whether it can be fully achieve or not, efforts must be made collectively. This responsibility cannot rest solely with the MACC. Instead, the government, private sector, schools, families and the wider community must all play their part," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia's key index close slightly higher at midday
Article:

Title: Woman killed in three-car crash near school in Tasek Gelugor
Article:
TASEK GELUGOR: A 60-year-old woman was killed in a three-car crash near SK Padang Menora here this morning.
The victim, identified as Zuraini Jaafar, was trapped in her Perodua Kancil following the collision involving a Perodua Axia and a Proton Saga at 8.26am.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said firefighters from the Tasek Gelugor station were dispatched to the scene and arrived at 8.41am.
"Three people were involved in the crash. Two victims were trapped in their vehicles, but one had already been extricated by the public before firefighters arrived.
"Our personnel used special rescue equipment to free the remaining trapped victim, who was pinned in the driver's seat. She was extricated at 9.13am and was pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel," he said.
John said the victim's body was handed over to police before being transported by a Health Ministry ambulance to Kepala Batas Hospital.
The Perodua Axia driver, a 69-year-old man, suffered minor injuries, while the Proton Saga driver, 51, was unhurt.
A total of nine firefighters, assisted by a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle, were involved in the operation, which concluded at 10.19am.
Police are investigating the cause of the crash.

Title: South Korean stocks collapse amid Asian tech rout
Article:
HONG KONG; South Korean stocks suffered one of their steepest plunges on Wednesday, with the bloodletting that has battered chip firms over the past month deepening as nervous investors unwound their bets on the AI boom.
The tech sector came under assault as traders fretted over the mesmerising sums being pumped into artificial intelligence, with investors questioning whether firms' lofty expectations would be met.
After a two-year rally that has seen several markets and companies around the world hit record highs, the air is blowing out, with chip firms bearing the brunt of the selling.
And Seoul was again on the frontline, with the Kospi plunging more than 12 per cent at one point to extend Tuesday's near-11 per cent collapse as chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung were hammered.
SK Hynix was crushed, shedding almost 20 per cent, having dived more than 14 per cent on Tuesday. It has now lost more than 50 per cent since hitting a record high a month ago. Samsung plunged more than 12 per cent.
The latest bout of selling in SK Hynix came after its April-June operating profit and revenue came in below expectations, even as net profit soared a forecast-beating 1,242 per cent.
The firm is a specialist supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips to US industry behemoth Nvidia, and a pillar of South Korea's tech-led economy.
Josh Gilbert, of eToro, said: "When you're the dominant supplier of the high-bandwidth memory that powers Nvidia's chips, the AI boom lands directly on your bottom line.
"That means the market is unlikely to focus on the headline numbers alone. The bigger question is whether margins and guidance can justify its recent performance."
Tokyo was also hit, diving around three per cent as chip firm Kioxia plunged 13 per cent, while Tokyo Electron was down 12 per cent.
Taipei gave up five per cent, with market heavyweight chipmaker TSMC down four per cent.
But while Shanghai and Jakarta also fell, the rest of Asia enjoyed gains, with Hong Kong up more than one per cent as its tech sector, which suffered a painful first half of the year, led the way. Sydney, Singapore, Wellington, Manila and Mumbai were also up.
Samsung is due to report earnings on Thursday, while Kioxia and US titans Microsoft, Meta, Apple and Amazon are also set to announce.
Oil traders were also suffering as volatility returned to the crude market after US and Saudi warplanes carried out strikes on Tuesday against Iran-backed militants in Iraq who launched more than two dozen drone attacks in recent days, the US military said.
The strikes targeted "Iran-aligned terrorists that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) directed to attack US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure", US Central Command announced in a statement.
CENTCOM had said earlier that Tehran launched multiple ballistic missiles in an "attempted surprise attack on US forces based in the Middle East", but they were all intercepted.
Iran on Wednesday said it had halted three oil tankers in the strait, through which a fifth of global crude and gas usually pass.
The strikes ended three days of calm after the US and Iran held off attacks, following almost two weeks of nightly US strikes on Iran and repeated missile and drone salvos targeting Washington's allies around the Gulf.
Both main oil contracts rose more than four per cent on Wednesday. Brent has swung wildly this month, surging from around US$72 at the start of July to more than US$100 last week, before the three-day pause.
The latest developments highlight the fragility of any efforts to find a lasting peace, even though US President Donald Trump this week said there was a "good chance" of a deal.
Wednesday also sees the Fed conclude its two-day meeting, and while most traders expect it to hold interest rates, there are concerns it could spring a surprise.
Uncertainty has been fuelled by new boss Kevin Warsh's refusal to publicly share his views on the economic outlook, part of his proposed reforms to reduce the amount of forward guidance the central bank offers.
Investors remain on edge, even after recent data suggested inflation was easing, the jobs market was softening and oil prices had come down.
"Assuming the Fed leaves rates unchanged as expected, traders will be on the lookout for a potentially stronger description of inflation risks and/or possible wording to signal conditional tightening," said Matt Weller at City Index.
But he said "Warsh has expressed scepticism towards such forward-looking comments in the past".
"Crucially, at least a couple of FOMC members are likely to favour an immediate interest rate increase, dissenting against the majority if necessary," he added.
"A third (or fourth) dissent in favour of hiking rates now would certainly represent a credible hawkish surprise and could boost the US dollar at the expense of risk assets."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Toyota to halt operations at 3 southern Japan plants through Friday after earthquake
Article:
TOKYO: Toyota will suspend operations at three plants in the southern region of Kyushu from the second production shift on Wednesday through Friday due to the impact of an earthquake in the area, the automaker said in a statement.
"The situation, including aftershocks and recovery efforts, is changing daily.
"We will continue to prioritise safety above all else in our responses and decisions," Toyota said.

Title: Forest City backs permanent police presence after scam syndicates busted
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Forest City has expressed support for a permanent police presence within the township, days after a joint enforcement operation dismantled two online scam syndicates operating from its apartments and bungalows.
In a statement, Forest City commended the police, Home Ministry, Immigration Department and other enforcement agencies for the operation, saying it reflected the government's comitment to upholding the rule of law and combating organised crime.
"Forest City fully supports these efforts and remains committed to maintaining a safe, secure and responsibly managed township in full compliance with Malaysian laws," the company said, adding that it had extended its full cooperation to the authorities throughout the operation.
It was previously reported that 335 suspects were arrested during simultaneous raids on 27 apartment units and five bungalows in Forest City on July 15 after Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the
operation
dismantled two syndicates involved in fake cryptocurrency investment and love scams targeting victims overseas.
Forest City said it welcomed the establishment of a permanent police presence within the township, saying a dedicated police station or service centre would strengthen crime prevention, improve emergency response and provide more accessible policing for residents, businesses and visitors.
"As Forest City continues to develop as an international duty-free township with a strategic location, an attractive living environment and increasing visitor and business activity, the company believes there is merit in strengthening long-term community policing," it said.
The company added that it remained committed to working with the government and enforcement agencies to uphold the rule of law, describing itself as a master-planned township founded on sustainable development, quality living and responsible governance.

Title: UBS logs forecast-beating quarterly profit, flags US$3 billion in new buybacks by end-June
Article:
ZURICH: UBS booked a 17 per cent jump in second-quarter profit on Wednesday, ahead of expectations, and said it plans to buy back shares worth US$3 billion by the middle of next year at the latest.
Of that amount, it intends to repurchase at least US$1 billion of shares over the next three months.
Net profit attributable to shareholders for Switzerland's biggest bank came in at US$2.8 billion, compared with a forecast of US$2.39 billion in a company-provided poll of analysts.
Its performance was driven by growth in wealth management and its investment bank, with the trading division delivering a record second quarter, UBS said.
The share buyback plans follow US$3 billion worth of buybacks completed in July. Analysts had forecast UBS would conduct some US$4.45 billion worth of buybacks during 2026.
UBS reiterated that the amount and pace of buybacks would depend on its short-term financial performance as well as the outcome of Swiss banking rules being debated in response to the 2023 collapse of Credit Suisse and its subsequent takeover by UBS.
Concerned about the risks to the Swiss economy should UBS collapse, the government has sought to make the bank hold around US$20 billion in additional Common Equity Tier 1 capital, a stance that UBS has said is excessive and would damage it competitively.
Lawmakers are expected to water down that requirement as they begin drafting the bill next month, as many fear requiring a permanent buffer of this scale could scare off UBS' investors.

Title: Bukit Aman announces 25 senior cop transfers, promotions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Federal police have announced the transfer and promotion of 25 senior officers, effective Sept 1.
The exercise involves Perlis police chief Deputy Commissioner Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim, who has been promoted to Commissioner of Police and appointed Internal Security and Public Order (Operations) deputy director at Bukit Aman.
Muhammad is scheduled to assume his new role on Aug 3.
Bukit Aman Special Branch E6 principal assistant director Deputy Commissioner Datuk Mohd Taufik Toh Abdullah will also be promoted to Commissioner of Police as Special Branch 1 deputy director.
Bukit Aman CID (D7) Organised Crime/Detention/Supervision principal assistant director Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Farouk Eshak will serve as Bukit Aman CID Forensic/Strategic Planning deputy director with the acting rank of Deputy Commissioner.
Two other Senior Assistant Commissioners elevated to Acting Deputy Commissioner are Sabah Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department chief Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin, who becomes Sabah deputy police commissioner, and Bukit Aman Special Branch E4A assistant director Roslan Alias, who takes over as Bukit Aman Special Branch E6 principal assistant director.
Sarawak CID chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Lim San Aik will assume the post of Sabah Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department chief, maintaining his current rank.
Bukit Aman Secretariat head Datuk Mohamad Noor Yusof Ali said 13 Assistant Commissioners have also been promoted to Senior Assistant Commissioner in new postings.
They include Dang Wangi district police chief Sazalee Adam, who has been named Kuala Lumpur CID chief, and Sentul district police chief Basri Sagoni, who will head Bukit Aman CID (D7) Organised Crime/Detention/Supervision.
Kuala Lumpur CID (Intelligence/Operations) deputy chief Zulkarnain Samsudin will assume the role of Selangor CID chief.
"Also promoted to Senior Assistant Commissioner are Kuala Lumpur Special Branch (Intelligence and Operations) deputy chief Kamaruzaman Md Alib as Bukit Aman Special Branch E1A assistant director, and Kuala Lumpur Narcotics CID chief Haslah Bachok as Bukit Aman Integrity and Standard Compliance Department (Operations/Intelligence) principal assistant director," Mohamad Noor said in a statement today.
Additionally, Iskandar Puteri district police chief Kumarasan Muniandy will take over as Sarawak CID chief.

Title: Rohingya refugees relocated to KL, Selangor, Penang after police documentation process [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 113 Rohingya refugees brought to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters after being relocated from outside the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office have been moved to new accommodation in Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Penang.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the documentation and identity verification exercise was conducted at Dataran Wira within the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters from 12.01am to 4.30pm on Tuesday.
He said representatives from the Malaysian Relief Agency (MRA) were also present to provide lunch and conduct basic health checks on the refugees during the exercise.
"Between 2pm and 4pm, 109 Rohingya refugees, together with one Indonesian woman who is the wife of the Rohingya community leader, one Iraqi refugee and one Somali refugee, were released in stages after their identities and documents were reverified.
"They were transported to destinations determined by non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the UNHCR," he said in a statement today.
Fadil said the refugees were released in stages through the main entrance of the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters after their identities were matched with their respective documents.
He said the group travelled to three destinations — Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Penang — with most using e-hailing services to reach their destinations.
"The destinations were based on where they have relatives or acquaintances who could accommodate them," he said.
Of the 113 people, 66 were
relocated
to Kuala Lumpur, 29 to Selangor and 18 to Penang.
The latest development follows the group's overnight stay at the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters after they were brought there from outside the UNHCR office in Jalan Bukit Petaling, where they had gathered after being evicted from their settlement in Kampung Kuala Muda, Kedah.
Police had earlier confirmed that all 113 people possessed valid UNHCR documentation, while Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said refugees holding UNHCR cards could remain in Malaysia on humanitarian grounds, although they remained subject to Malaysian laws.
